electrolysisInfo.title: What Is Electrolysis
electrolysisInfo.paragraphOne: Electrolysis is a hair removal treatment. A trained electrologist inserts a thin wire into the hair follicle under the surface of the skin. An electric current moves down the wire to the bottom of the follicle, destroying the hair root. The follicle damage prevents hair from growing and causes the existing hair to fall out.
electrolysisInfo.paragraphTwo: Electrolysis has been around for more than 100 years. It was first invented to remove irritating ingrown eyelash hairs. Electrolysis is the only FDA-approved method for permanent hair removal.

about.title: About Me
about.description:
My name is Daria Zhuravel, certified electrologist and founder of PulseBeauty Studio in Auckland, New Zealand.

My professional journey began in 2016 — not as a practitioner, but as a client. Experiencing electrolysis personally allowed me to see its true transformative power. I discovered not only a permanent solution to unwanted hair, but also the confidence and freedom that come with feeling comfortable in your own skin. That moment defined my future path.

Determined to master this craft at the highest level, I began my professional education in 2018, training with leading experts in Moscow. In 2019, I further advanced my qualifications in Dnipro, Ukraine, deepening both my theoretical knowledge and practical precision.

Committed to excellence and continuous growth, I completed an advanced professional development course in 2025, refining my techniques and staying aligned with the latest international standards in electrolysis.

Today, at PulseBeauty Studio in Auckland, I provide discreet, safe, and highly personalized electrolysis treatments for women and men of all skin and hair types. I work exclusively with modern equipment and sterile single-use tools, maintaining the highest standards of hygiene and professional care.

For me, beauty is not about trends or standards — it is about confidence, comfort, and self-assurance. My mission is to deliver permanent results with precision, care, and respect for every client’s individuality.

list.name: Electrolysis on the Face
list.photoCaption: Face area - Upper lip, chin, ears, cheeks, and between the brows. Removes fine and coarse hair for a smooth, confident look.
list.description:
Facial electrolysis is one of the most effective and permanent methods of removing unwanted hair.
The duration of a session can vary from 15 to 60 minutes, depending on the treated area and hair density.

A full course usually takes 1.5 to 2 years with regular appointments. This is due to the natural hair growth cycles - electrolysis targets each follicle individually, ensuring permanent results over time.

Before the Procedure
• Hair length should be about 2-3 mm so the specialist can work precisely.
• Avoid sun exposure, tanning beds, and aggressive cosmetic treatments (peels, scrubs) for at least 3-5 days before your session.
• Do not pluck or wax hairs between appointments - shaving or trimming is allowed if necessary.

After the Procedure
• Mild redness or sensitivity is normal and usually subsides within a few hours.
• Avoid overheating (saunas, gyms, hot baths) for 24-48 hours.
• Use a gentle antiseptic and soothing cream recommended by your specialist.

Electrolysis on the face is suitable for any hair color and skin type - it works where laser hair removal may be ineffective.

list.name: Electrolysis for Underarms
list.photoCaption: Underarm area - Keeps underarms permanently clean and smooth for lasting comfort.
list.description:
Electrolysis in the underarm area is a reliable way to permanently remove unwanted hair and forget about constant shaving or painful waxing.

The first session usually lasts 60-120 minutes.
A full course takes about 1.5 to 2 years with regular visits, depending on natural hair growth cycles.

Before the Procedure
• Hair length should be around 2-3 mm.
• Avoid tanning, sunbeds, and aggressive skincare treatments a few days before your session.
• Do not use deodorants or antiperspirants on the day of your appointment.

After the Procedure
• Mild redness or sensitivity may occur but usually disappears within a few hours.
• Avoid heat exposure (sauna, gym, hot baths) for 24-48 hours.
• For 1-2 days, apply a gentle antiseptic and soothing cream recommended by your specialist.

Electrolysis for underarms ensures perfectly smooth skin forever and is effective for any hair type or color.

list.name: Electrolysis for Legs
list.photoCaption: Legs - Permanent smoothness for all hair types, no more shaving or waxing.
list.description:
Electrolysis on the legs is a permanent solution to unwanted hair, allowing you to enjoy smooth skin without shaving or waxing.

The first session may last 2 to 4 hours (depending on whether you choose lower legs or full legs).
A full course takes approximately 1.5-2 years with regular visits, as it works through the natural hair growth cycles.

Before the Procedure
• Hair length should be about 2-3 mm.
• Avoid sunburn, tanning beds, and aggressive cosmetic treatments for several days before your session.
• Do not pluck or wax hairs between treatments (only shaving or trimming is allowed).

After the Procedure
• Mild redness or sensitivity may appear but usually fades within a few hours.
• Avoid heavy workouts, hot baths, or saunas for 24-48 hours.
• For the first days, use a gentle antiseptic and soothing cream as recommended by your specialist.

Electrolysis for legs is suitable for all hair colors and skin types, guaranteeing permanently smooth skin.

list.name: Electrolysis for Bikini Area
list.photoCaption: Bikini area - Classic, deep, or full bikini for smooth, confident skin.
list.description:
Electrolysis in the bikini area is an effective and safe method for permanent hair removal. The procedure helps eliminate irritation from shaving or painful waxing, leaving the skin perfectly smooth.

The first session lasts from 1 to 7 hours, depending on the chosen area.
A full course takes approximately 1.5-2 years with regular visits to the specialist.

Types of Bikini Electrolysis
• Classic Bikini - hair removal along the underwear line.
• Deep Bikini - removal of hair along the sides and partially inside the intimate area.
• Full (Total) Bikini - complete removal of hair in the entire intimate zone.

Before the Procedure
• Hair length should be around 2-3 mm.
• Avoid tanning, sunburn, and aggressive skin treatments for several days before your session.
• Do not apply creams or oils on the day of the procedure.

After the Procedure
• Mild redness or skin sensitivity is normal and usually disappears within a few hours.
• Avoid pools, hot baths, exercise, and tight synthetic underwear for 24-48 hours.
• Use a gentle antiseptic and soothing cream as recommended by your specialist.

Electrolysis for the bikini area is suitable for all hair types and guarantees long-lasting comfort and confidence.

aftercare.title: Care tips and contraindications
aftercare.description:
To ensure the best results and skin comfort after your electrolysis session:

• Avoid sun exposure for 24-48 hours.
• Do not touch or scratch the treated area.
• Apply soothing cream as recommended.
• Avoid hot showers, saunas, and intense workouts for 24 hours.
• Use gentle, fragrance-free skincare products.

items.question: Who is electrolysis for?
items.answer: It can be used on most people including men and women who want body hair removed for cosmetic reasons, women who are suffering from hirsuitism (excess hair in a male pattern), which can be caused by the menopause, conditions such as polycystic ovary syndrome or steroid use, and clients who are undergoing gender reassignment from male to female.

items.question: Who can't have electrolysis?
items.answer:
Conditions that may prevent treatment include: haemophilia, heart disorders, pacemakers, cochlear implant, contagious diseases and disorders, Hepatitis B, HIV, cancer or epilepsy.

Conditions that may restrict treatment: steroid drugs, endocrine disorders, metal plates and pins, cardiovascular disorders, loss of tactile sensation in localised areas, skin disorders and diseases, nickel allergy, hairy moles, pregnancy, drugs/alcohol, cuts/abrasions/bruising, emotional problems, dermagraphic skin condition, microdermabrasion or dermabrasion, chemical peels, latex allergy (wear vinyl gloves), certain medications or creams, breast implants (contra-indication to underarm treatment), epilepsy, diabetes, psoriasis, eczema, acne, dermabrasion on the areas to be treated.

items.question: How many treatments are needed?
items.answer: For optimal results, several treatments and after-care advice are usually offered over a period of weeks to several months or longer.

items.question: How does electrolysis work?
items.answer:
The procedure involves inserting a very fine, disposable, sterile probe (the same diameter as the hair) into the hair follicle, which is a natural opening in the skin. The current is then skilfully discharged into the hair follicle. The client's only sensation is heat passing down the probe to the base of the follicle.

The follicles are destroyed using either heat (thermolysis) or a chemical reaction (galvanic), or both combined (with the blend). The treatment can be tailored to each client's skin, hair, and pain tolerance.

During a course of treatments, there will be a constant, gradual decrease in hair growth until it is completely removed. The number of treatments required will vary depending on the individual and is discussed during the initial consultation.

Any part of the body can be treated with electrolysis. The first sign that electrolysis is working is that the hair grows softer, finer, and lighter in colour.

items.question: What's the difference between electrolysis and laser?
items.answer:
Electrolysis uses a very fine, disposable, sterile probe to permanently destroy each hair follicle's ability to reproduce, resulting in complete permanent removal after a course of treatment.

Laser and IPL usually provide permanent hair reduction rather than full permanent removal in a treated area. They can be helpful for some people but are often less suitable for certain hair colours, skin tones, and medication profiles.

Electrolysis may take longer overall, but it is used when permanent removal of all treated hair is the goal.

items.question: How many treatments do I need?
items.answer:
The number of treatments varies by client because hair density, growth cycles, hair thickness, skin sensitivity, and treatment area all differ.

Most areas require regular appointments over an extended period, often at least a year or more. Session lengths can range from around 30 minutes to several hours depending on the area being treated.

You'll usually notice progressive improvement throughout the treatment plan rather than only at the end.

items.question: Does electrolysis hurt?
items.answer:
Electrolysis is not completely painless, but sensation is typically manageable. Most clients describe it as brief heat, a pinprick, or a mild sting when current is applied.

Sensitivity can vary by area; for example, the upper lip is often more sensitive.

Treatment settings can be adjusted to suit individual comfort and tolerance.

items.question: Which areas can be treated by electrolysis?
items.answer:
Apart from the inner ear, virtually any area can be treated.

Common facial areas include upper lip, chin, neck, cheeks, brows, between brows, nose, and hairline. Body areas often include chest, nipples, abdomen, underarms, arms, shoulders, bikini line, buttocks, fingers, and toes.

Electrolysis can be used across all skin colours and hair types.

items.question: Can I have electrolysis if I'm pregnant?
items.answer:
Pregnancy is not usually a contraindication to thermolysis/shortwave diathermy electrolysis.

However, treatment of breast and abdominal areas is usually avoided in later stages due to skin sensitivity and stretching.

Blend/galvanic approaches are often avoided during pregnancy. If unsure which method is being used, discuss this with your practitioner and healthcare provider.

items.question: I want electrolysis but I can't bear the thought of letting the hair grow between appointments. What can I do?
items.answer:
Between appointments, hair can still be managed by cutting or shaving, including facial areas.

Hair generally does not need to be very long for treatment, so your practitioner can guide you on suitable length before each session.

items.question: What does the skin look like following treatment?
items.answer:
Immediately after treatment there is often temporary redness and localized swelling, depending on skin sensitivity.

By the next day, most people see only minor signs. Some may notice tiny reddish-brown pinprick scabs, especially where hairs are distorted or ingrown. These typically heal and shed naturally over days to about a week.

items.question: Why shouldn't I wax, tweeze, thread, or epilate during treatment?
items.answer:
Electrolysis is recognized as a permanent hair-removal method.

Methods that remove hair from the root (waxing, tweezing, threading, epilating) can interfere with treatment consistency and may stimulate stronger regrowth over time in some cases.

If you need interim management, shaving/cutting is usually preferred because these methods do not remove the root.

items.question: Is there a good time to start electrolysis treatment?
items.answer:
It is best to start when you can maintain regular appointments.

Avoid beginning right before long travel, very busy periods, or major events if those would interrupt the treatment schedule.

You should still see progressive reduction during the course, which helps keep motivation high.
